heading: The real price of industrial commodities
plot_title: Real commodity prices fell from 100 in 1900 to 35 in 2000, then rose to 84 in 2011
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: Jacks (2019), ["From Boom to Bust: A Typology of Real Commodity Prices in the Long Run"](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11698-018-0173-5), *Cliometrica* 13(2), data file "Real commodity prices, 1850–2020" ([archived copy of the author's data page](https://web.archive.org/web/20221007161341/http://www.sfu.ca/~djacks/data/boombust/)), for 1900–2020; extended to 2025 with the [World Bank, Commodity Price Data (The Pink Sheet)](https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/commodity-markets), deflated by the [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (`CPIAUCSL`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL). The textbook's figure uses proprietary Global Financial Data, so our index is built from these open sources instead.
Prepared file: [`data/ch06/fig6-5.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch06/fig6-5.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch06/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 6.5 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: A slowdown in U.S. economic growth?
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 6 with a precomputed slider for the number of years in the average
plot_title: 10-year average growth of GDP per person: 2.2% in 1960–2006, 1.2% since 2009
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Real Gross Domestic Product (`GDPCA`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPCA) and [U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Population (`B230RC0A052NBEA`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/B230RC0A052NBEA); recessions from the [NBER based Recession Indicators (`USREC`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/USREC), which follow the [NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee](https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating).
Prepared files: [`data/ch06/us_gdp_pc.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch06/us_gdp_pc.csv), [`data/ch06/recessions.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch06/recessions.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch06/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 6.6 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: A slowdown in U.S. economic growth?

source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [Penn World Table 11.0](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/), Groningen Growth and Development Centre ([DOI 10.34894/FABVLR](https://doi.org/10.34894/FABVLR)), variables `rgdpna` (real GDP at constant national prices) and `pop` (population); cite as Feenstra, Inklaar and Timmer (2015), ["The Next Generation of the Penn World Table"](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20130954), *American Economic Review* 105(10).
